_comment: RAER submission template — copy this file, rename it RAER-<year>-<seq>.json, fill every field, and open a PR. The shown enum fields carry one VALID example value each; the allowed sets are verdict.claimedVerdict ∈ {EXECUTION_EVIDENCE_ADMISSIBLE, FIXTURE_REJECTED, UNKNOWN}, claimedAdmissibility ∈ {admissible, rejected, none}, matchesBundle ∈ {match, mismatch-or-none}. The CI contract (test/ci/raer-registry.test.js) validates structure: a submission that cannot parse records UNKNOWN — it is never counted as a rejection of the incident (fail-closed, per registry.json#validationMatrix).

incident.title: Short neutral title — what happened, no adjectives
incident.summary: 2-5 sentences. Facts only. Allegations stay attributed ('the lab reported…'), never asserted by this registry.
incident.summaryAr: ملخص بالعربية عند توفره — نفس قواعد الحياد
incident.reportedBy: the party reporting (lab / regulator / auditor / affected party) — the registry records WHO, and validates nothing about their claim

evidenceBundle.bundlePath: docs/raer/bundles/<id>/ — committed tree path holding the AIE-1 evidence bundle (commit-anchored: what is registered is what was committed)
evidenceBundle.bundleSha256: <sha256 over the bundle bytes; the replay re-computes this and any mismatch is a named finding>
evidenceBundle.assembleHow: the documented AIE-1 assembly one-liner (docs/agent-incident-evidence.md) — a reviewer reproduces the bundle from the same records

verdict.verdictNote: why the submitter believes this verdict — the engine decides admissibility, never conformity

replay.executedBy: who ran the replay (maintainer CI / independent party) — an entry reaches REPLAYED only after a CI-executed replay reproduces the claimed verdict on the recorded bundleSha256
replay.transcript: path to the replay transcript committed beside the bundle (stdout of the verify run: same bytes in → byte-identical verdict out)
